newsitem.title: USA: Hawaii Gov proposes $1 bln capital projects budget.
newsitem.headline: Hawaii Gov proposes $1 bln capital projects budget.

text.p: Hawaii Gov. Ben Cayetano on Tuesday proposed a $1 billion, two-year capital improvement projects budget, designed to "kick start" the state's economy, the governor's office said.

"This one-time infusion will kick start the economy by accelerating the design and construction of needed infrastructure such as public schools, university facilities, libraries and other projects now rather than years down the line," Cayetano's office said in a statement.

The $1 billion building budget -- two-and-a-half times the size of the usual budget for state construction -- did not include highway and airport projects by the state Department of Transportation, the governor said.
The proposal was part of the administration's package of over 200 bills for consideration by the state legislature.

Cayetano also proposed a measure that would establish a state "rainy day" fund for use during budget emergencies, and a bill that would consolidate the functions of the Hawaii Housing Authority, Hawaii Finance and Development Corp and the Rental Housing Trust Fund Commission.
As outlined in his State of the State address earlier this month, the governor proposed tax relief to encourage hotel renovation, help first-time home buyers and boost the economy.
One of these measures would provide for income tax relief of 25 percent to 100 percent for low-income families earning less than $22,000 a year.
In addition, the governor proposed bills to regulate and license retail tobacco vendors and increase the cigarette excise tax from three cents to five cents.
